newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Mark sales boost lev supply on Bulgaria depo mkt.
newsitem.headline: Mark sales boost lev supply on Bulgaria depo mkt.

text.p: Interbank deposit rates on the Bulgarian money market remained steady in thin trade as supply of funds topped demand on the second day of operation of the currency board system, dealers said.
"Demand for lev is very low while supply rose from Tuesday after people sold their cheaply bought marks before the introduction of the currency board," said a bank dealer.

Traders said that banks have sold marks to the central bank in order to profit from forex transaction costs. The mark ask levels were between 900 and 950 levs in the weeks before the currency baord launch.
The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs and selling at 1,000 levs in line with fixed exchange rate regime launched on Tuesday.
Overnight interbank depo rates stood at 9-10 percent annually, flat from Tuesday, while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 7-8 percent, also unchanged.
The simple annual main interest rate is now set at 10.12 percent by the central bank.
